title: The Lamp on the Wire: film finale for orchestra
brief: Music for the climax of an animated feature film, for the largest orchestra the banks give. It opens with the film's main theme on one instrument (the piano), builds through a chase, a moment where everything stops and a return to the largest statement of the theme by the whole orchestra, and lets it go quietly. One-shot cue, no dialogue over it, a ring-out ending. Every section of the orchestra carries the theme.

sections.intent: The theme alone on the piano, one key at a time, as it was once typed out; C major.
The walk along the hedge top: woodwinds take the theme over harp and pizzicato, the strings sing its second strain, a horn begins it again and the gust bends its last note.
The lamp is torn away: tremolo and harp sweeps on the dominant of A minor, quickening.

The chase down the telegraph wire: a typewriter ostinato (bell and carriage return every fourth bar), the theme in A minor in the brass at its old speed, a struggle that climbs by semitones, the wire snaps.
The reef, then everything stops: one struck Lydian chord, a ring, one held high note, and the theme in bells and a muted horn over still strings, A-flat major.
The return: the head of the theme in the cellos, then violas and horn, then violins and woodwinds, a whole tone higher each time (A-flat, B-flat, C), and a dominant pedal that breathes once.
The whole orchestra: the theme in D major, its second strain, and the last phrase carried up to the held high D while the brass and timpani give the head under it.
It is let go: the piano alone again, a minor subdominant, one flute leap, the lamp a bell among stars.

association.whole: At dusk a girl takes a stroll along the top of the harbour hedge with a paper lamp that wears a star decal, humming the tune her grandmother used to tap out on a typewriter. A gust tears the lamp away and she rides after it down the telegraph wire in a burlap sack, keeping her grip while the line clatters like keys, bell and carriage return, until the wire snaps over the reef. Everything stops: under the water the lamp sinks in light the colour of sorbet. She lifts her chin, the town's lamps answer one by one, and the lamp is ladled up into the sky, the seventh star of the Dipper, the ladle that points at the pole star.

gives.what: the eight scenes in the order of the story: stroll, hedge, gust, wire, reef, chin, ladle, star

the theme's head is a ladle of seven notes: a handle of three (two alike and a step up), a bowl that dips, and a leap of a sixth that points up, as the Dipper points at the pole star; the note it points at, the high D, is reached only in the last phrase of the tutti
gives.where: bars 1-2 and every statement; the high D in bars 81-85

gives.what: the typewriter: sixteenth-note clatter in 3+3+2, a triangle bell at the end of every fourth bar and a ratchet and falling run for the carriage return; the theme sails over it in doubled note values, at the speed of the stroll

the reef and the sorbet are one chord in two lights, a major seventh with a Lydian fourth: struck hard on F (bar 51), floating on A-flat under the bells (bar 54); the return climbs by whole tones, A-flat, B-flat, C, to D
gives.where: reef bars 51-56, chin bars 57-66, the peak bars 81-83

gives.what: the wire is one held high note on a solo violin, always the fifth of the key; the lamp is a glockenspiel; the keys are claves and a slit drum; the grip is the brass hammering the handle; the first and last voice is the piano, the instrument with keys

plan.identity: One theme whose head is seven notes, a handle, a bowl and a leap that points up; the piece is the story of that leap: bent down by the gust, set in minor on the wire, hung in bells, raised three times by a whole tone, and answered at last by the high D it pointed at.

high_point.means: the melody's highest held notes (D6, E6, D6) kept for bars 81-85, over B-flat and C major chords the piece has not used at that level (flat VI, flat VII, I), the bass at its lowest, the whole brass and timpani giving the head under the held notes, clash cymbals and bells; a bar of thinner woodwind writing and one beat of air before it

sections.differs: other instruments for the first time: the theme passes to the woodwinds, its second strain to the strings
no theme, only its handle snatched by the woodwinds; one dominant, tremolo, the tempo quickening
fast, minor, short notes; the theme in the brass in doubled values over an ostinato
after one struck chord almost nothing: bells, a muted horn, still strings, a pedal
the bass moves again; the head three times, a whole tone higher and with more players each time
everyone; the theme whole for the first time since the hedge, in a new key, and its last leap completed
the piano alone again over held strings; the cadence turns through the minor subdominant

decisions: Style: orchestral/cinematic alone. Its map leaves tempo and rhythm without a source, so those are this piece's own: a walking 72-76 for the theme, 132 for the chase, 58 for the still scene; the mix follows orchestration.md (wide dynamics, one hall).

Keys: C major for the theme alone and its first setting, A minor for the chase, A-flat for the still scene (a third below C, reached from the F chord of the reef), then A-flat, B-flat, C, D by whole tones, so the tutti stands a tone above the opening and its flat VI and flat VII (B-flat, C) are the keys the return has just passed through.
The theme is pentatonic except for one F in its sixth bar (a 9-8 over the subdominant, then the major seventh held): the one semitone is kept for the phrase's peak.
Missing instruments: no English horn, contrabassoon, celesta or choir in the banks; a bass clarinet and the bass trombone take the lowest wind lines, glockenspiel and vibraphone the bell colours.

Soft solos have parts of their own (piano_solo, fl_solo, ob_solo, cl_solo, hn_solo, hn_mute, glock_solo, vn_solo) beside the tutti parts of the same instruments, since a part is levelled from its louder passages; from round 3 the soft passages of second violins, violas and cellos have parts of their own too (vn2_soft, va_soft, vc_soft).

How near: c80_db 7, between the guide's clear starting point (+16) and a hall (+2 to -2): the tutti is meant to sound large, the chase has fast figures that must stay legible, and the still scene needs the room around few notes.
range_lu 13: a film cue with a solo piano opening and a full tutti; the master keeps most of that distance but lifts the soft scenes enough for ordinary playback.

vertical: the collisions left are of four kinds, all meant, checked bar by bar: (1) the ninth of the dominant, F, above its root E in the gust and on the pedal of bars 47-50 (tremolo, horns and trumpets over the bass: a dominant minor ninth voiced as usual); (2) the flat sixth of the handle, F, hammered by the low brass and snatched by the woodwinds against E, the grip of the story; (3) the struck chord of the reef, a major seventh with a Lydian fourth, voiced as a low cluster on purpose; (4) the passing G of the tune itself over the F-sharp of the G major ninth chord in bars 72 and 80, an eighth note long. The accidental ones (harp notes ringing into the next chord, held strings under the suspensions of the tune in bars 14, 19, 54, 58, 65-66 and 77) were rewritten before the first render.

parallels: what is left is doubling, not two voices: timpani and staccato bassoons on the roots of the bass ostinato, a line doubled at the unison or octave by another instrument for part of a phrase (flute and clarinet, horns and cellos, trumpets, the woodwinds on the tune), and in bar 50 the brass handle against the chromatic run for one sixteenth. The outer voices of the last cadence move in contrary motion.

low_intervals: in the chase the low brass doubles the hammered handle an octave down against the bass ostinato (fifths and fourths, and tritones on the diminished chords, under B-flat 2): a dark, crowded low register is the sound of the struggle and lasts eight bars; the chord of the reef is a low cluster on purpose. The harp, the pads and the glissandi of the tutti were re-spaced above their limits; the few left there are a semitone or two under (a fourth A2-D3, a third B2-D3) between the pad of the trombones and the bass doubled at the octave.

plan:hedge: kept as planned. The hedge is written a step louder than the piano alone (mean velocity 61 against 57) because round 1 measured its harp 13 dB under the flute and the harp was raised; the plan meant that nothing rises before the gust, and the measured levels say so (the hedge 2.4 LU over the stroll, the gust 4 LU over the hedge).

plan:reef: kept as planned. In time the harmony is far slower there (6 chords in 25 seconds against 18 in 44); the review counts changes a bar, and a bar of the reef lasts 2.3 times a bar of the wire.

tracks.name: Claves, slit drum and ratchet (the typewriter)
